structure: Read the whole 30-line ruling file ruling-sam-2026-10-07.md in full. Lines 3-21 are Sam's verbatim quote in five paragraphs: goal (lines 3-5), the DR1 parity backlog's role with one elision marked [...] (lines 7-9), precedence (lines 11-13), decisions on questions for people (lines 15-17) and themes (lines 19-21). Lines 23-30 are the main session's reading as 8 numbered claims, all marked New. Each numbered claim was checked against the quote: all 8 are supported by it, one only by implication (the 'nothing is built because DR1 says so on its own' half of claim 3, and the 'over what the real services do today' framing of claim 5). Multi-fact claims are split into one claim per decision, and the gaps the ruling leaves open on what it touches are recorded as gap claims.

claims.statement: Wherever a real service differs from Design Release 2.1 of the GB notification service prototype, the real service changes to match Design Release 2.1.
claims.quote: Goal: wherever the real services differ from Design Release 2.1, they change to match it.
claims.note: New: answers no earlier report question.

claims.statement: Which repos change (frontends, backends and other repos) is worked out from the evidence, not fixed in advance.
claims.quote: Work out from the evidence which frontends, backends and other repos that touches.
claims.note: New. The 'not fixed in advance' reading follows from 'work out from the evidence'.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements.
claims.quote: The DR1 parity backlog. [...] It is not a source of requirements.

claims.statement: Nothing is built because the DR1 parity backlog says so on its own; this follows from the backlog not being a source of requirements and being usable only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-07.md lines 7-8 (DR1 paragraph); claim 3 second sentence
claims.quote: It is not a source of requirements. Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash
claims.note: New. The main session's claim 3 states this in so many words; the quote implies it.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is used only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.
claims.quote: Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash

claims.statement: Where DR1 already made a judgement on that same difference between the real frontend and the prototype, the DR1 judgement is followed.
claims.quote: if DR1 already made a judgement on that difference, follow it and cite the row.

claims.statement: Where a DR1 judgement is followed, the DR1 parity backlog row it comes from is cited.
claims.quote: follow it and cite the row.

claims.statement: The prototype (Design Release 2.1) wins by default over what the real services do today.
claims.quote: Precedence: the prototype wins by default.
claims.note: New. 'Over what the real services do today' is the main session's framing; it follows from the Goal paragraph.

claims.statement: A DR1 judgement on the same difference overrides the prototype default.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. 'On the same difference' comes from the DR1 paragraph (lines 8-9).

claims.statement: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default; the ruling names persistence, validation, authentication and cross-service behaviour as such constraints.
claims.quote: a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. The quote says 'auth'; claim 6 reads it as authentication. Claim 6 adds 'such as', making the list examples; the quote's parenthesis can be read either as examples or as the full list.

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.
